source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Wheels and Tires, p.10-6

procedures.title: Wheels: balance
steps: Static: correct with a commercial wheel balancer, following its instructions.
Dynamic: use a commercial dynamic balancer, which tells where to put weights.
First clear any debris from the wheel vent slots and wheel discs (especially mud that may have frozen).
To fix static balance without upsetting dynamic balance, split the needed weight half on the inner rim edge and half on the outer edge.
To fix dynamic balance without upsetting static balance, put half the weight on the rim opposite the heavy spot and the other half 180° away on the other side of the rim.
Balance wheels with wire wheel covers with the covers installed.
notes: Static unbalance causes front wheel pounding called tramp.
Dynamic (running) balance requires static balance plus smooth running about the wheel centerline.

procedures.title: Wheel run-out: check
steps: Measure side wobble on the side of the rim at the tire base; it must not exceed 1/16".
With the tire off, measure on the rim bead seat; the wheel must run true to the spindle within 1/16 inch.
If run-out is excessive, check for a bent or poorly mounted wheel, worn knuckle bearings or worn steering connections.

specs.what: lateral run-out at rim side (tire on)
radial run-out at bead seat (tire off)

notes: Run-out, eccentricity and balance relate closely to steering and front wheel alignment (see the suspension section).

procedures.title: Tire wear indicators: check
steps: Look for the indicator bands molded into the groove bottoms; they show as 1/2-inch wide bands at 1/16 inch tread depth.
Replace the tire when bands show in two or more neighboring grooves.
notes: See figure 8 in the manual (tread still good vs. worn out).

procedures.title: Tubeless tire: remove from rim
steps: Remove the valve cap and core and let all the air out.
Push the inner side of the tire down into the rim well with a bead loosening tool; if using tire irons, avoid damaging the bead sealing ribs.
With irons on the opposite side, lever the bead off in small bites around the rim.
notes: Caution: never use tire irons that have sharp edges or corners.
